items.stem: To solve 3x + 2y = 12 and 5x − 2y = 4 by elimination, what should you do first?
items.markingKey: The y-coefficients are +2 and −2, so adding eliminates y: 8x = 16.

items.stem: Explain how you decide whether to add or subtract two equations when using elimination.
items.answer: Make the coefficients of one variable equal in size. If they have the same sign, subtract; if they have opposite signs, add.
items.markingKey: B1 equal coefficients; B1 same sign subtract / opposite signs add [2]

items.stem: Explain why the equations 2x + 3y = 7 and 4x + 6y = 10 have no solution.
items.answer: Doubling the first gives 4x + 6y = 14, which contradicts 4x + 6y = 10; the lines are parallel and never meet.
items.markingKey: B1 compare multiples; B1 parallel/contradiction [2]

items.stem: Solve the simultaneous equations. Show your working. 5x + 6y = 69, 5x − y = 6
items.markingKey: M1 makes coefficients of one variable equal; M1 adds/subtracts correctly; A1 x = 3; A1 y = 9.

items.markingKey: M1 makes coefficients of one variable equal (multiplying one or both equations); M1 adds/subtracts correctly; A1 x = 0; A1 y = 4.

items.stem: A school group buys bottles of juice at a market in Lagos. 4 large and 3 small cost $41.00. 1 large and 6 small cost $26.00. Let the price of one large be $a and one small be $b. (a) Write down two equations in a and b. (b) The group has $120. They buy 4 large. Find the greatest number of small they can also buy.
Explain why substitution is a good method for y = 3x − 4 and 5x − 2y = 6.
items.answer: The first equation already gives y in terms of x, so it can be substituted directly into the second.
items.markingKey: B1 y is already the subject; B1 substitute into other equation [2]

items.stem: Explain how you can check a solution to a pair of simultaneous equations.
items.answer: Substitute both values into the equation not used in the final step (ideally both equations); each side must balance.
items.markingKey: B1 substitute values; B1 into both / the other equation [2]

items.stem: Solve 3x + 5y = 40 and 5x + 5y = 50. What is the value of x?
items.markingKey: Eliminate y, solve for x = 5 (y = 5).

Which is the quadratic formula for ax² + bx + c = 0?
items.markingKey: Standard formula; the whole numerator is divided by 2a.

items.stem: Explain why the equation x² + 4x + 9 = 0 has no real solutions.
items.answer: b² − 4ac = 16 − 36 = −20 < 0; there is no real square root of a negative number. Also (x + 2)² + 5 is always at least 5, so it is never 0.
items.markingKey: B1 discriminant negative (or completed square ≥ 5); B1 conclusion [2]

items.stem: Explain why a quadratic equation can have at most two solutions.
items.answer: Its graph is a parabola, which can cross a horizontal line (the x-axis) at most twice; equivalently the ± in the formula gives at most two values.
items.markingKey: B1 parabola/±; B1 at most two crossings [2]

items.stem: Jonas solves 2x² − 9x − 3 = 0 and writes x = 9 ± √105 ÷ 4, dividing only the square root by 4. Explain the error and give the correct solutions to 2 decimal places.
items.answer: The whole of −b ± √(b² − 4ac) must be divided by 2a. x = 4.81 or x = −0.31.

items.stem: Explain why the inequality sign must be reversed when dividing both sides by a negative number. Use 2 < 5 as an example.
items.answer: 2 < 5 but −2 > −5: multiplying by −1 reverses the order of numbers on the number line, so the sign must be reversed.

items.stem: Explain why −3 < x < 5 can be written as a single statement but x < −3 or x > 5 cannot.

items.stem: Describe how to find the integer values that satisfy 7 ≤ 2n + 1 < 15.

items.stem: Explain how to decide which side of the line 3x + 2y = 12 represents 3x + 2y < 12.
items.answer: Test a point not on the line, such as (0, 0): 0 < 12 is true, so the region containing the origin is 3x + 2y < 12.
items.markingKey: B1 test a point; B1 conclusion [2]

items.stem: Explain why the line y = x is drawn broken for the region y > x but solid for y ≥ x.
items.answer: For y > x the points on the line (where y = x) are not included, shown by a broken line; for y ≥ x they are included, shown solid.
items.markingKey: B1 strict/not strict; B1 broken/solid meaning [2]

items.stem: Explain why (x + 6)/x cannot be simplified to 6 by cancelling the x.
